v1.feedback: Strong chain read — the ochre tower is clearly the substrate and psithurism drives three distinct layers (height-squared sway, high-freq rustle, lateral leaf-scatter dust) rather than one blanket effect. The h²×0.35 wind amplitude risks smearing the top of the column into an amorphous wobble at peak displacement; cap it or add a smoothstep ceiling around 0.2 so the silhouette stays columnar even mid-gust. The sage-copper tip color is a smart addition but may read as murky under additive blending on the dark background — try a slightly more saturated copper-green (0.42,0.50,0.22) so the autumn-canopy gradient actually lands at screen distance.

v2.feedback: The chain lineage reads clearly — ochre column is still the structural anchor and the psithurism overlay (height² sway, tip rustle, lateral leaf scatter) lands as wind colonizing stone rather than a fresh scene. The palette ramp from yellow-ochre through raw-sienna to sage-copper is restrained and earns the concept. Two refinements: the leaf-scatter particles feel disconnected from the tower surface — spawn them from actual tower vertex positions rather than a parametric shell so the wind appears to peel foliage off the form; and the rustle frequency (uTime*4.5) is uniform across all tip particles, producing a mechanical shimmer — add a second low-frequency modulator per-particle (seeded) so clusters of leaves phase in and out like real gusts catching different branches.
